# Theory: Content Addressing is the Whole Trick

Git is a content-addressed filesystem plus names. Internals are not trivia; they are why hosting, LFS, and `fsck` look the way they do.

## Invariants

1. Object name = hash of type + size + payload (SHA-1 historically, SHA-256 optional).
2. Blobs have no filename; trees bind names to hashes.
3. Packfiles are compression (deltas) of that object set, not the data model.
4. A server is constrained by quarantine, `receive.denyCurrentBranch`, and hook timing around these objects.

```text
commit → tree → blob
   \→ parent commit
packfile = many objects + delta chains  (disk, not mental model)
```

## What can break

- Editing files under `.git/objects` by hand.
- Assuming SHA-1 collision is a daily concern (it is a research/hosting concern).

## How to read this chapter

Object store, hashes, packfiles/`git log`, server-facing internals, `cat-file` lab.
